# E2E — generated by QACluster

BDD framework: **features (Gherkin) → step definitions → pages**, on Playwright + TypeScript with
[playwright-bdd](https://github.com/vitalets/playwright-bdd). Generated from the code (scenarios designed by TestGraph)
and stabilized by running it against the app. **It runs on its own: no QACluster or Claude needed.**

## Structure
```
e2e/
  src/main/                              # framework code
    pages/                               # Page Objects (locators + business intentions)
    fixtures/index.ts                    # DI: Pages + ScenarioContext as scenario-scoped fixtures; exports Given/When/Then
    support/ScenarioContext.ts           # state shared between steps of ONE scenario
    data/                                # test data + factories (unique per scenario)
    utils/                               # generic helpers
    reporters/summary-reporter.ts        # per-run summary
  src/test/                              # what is tested
    resources/features/<flow>/<flow>.feature   # Gherkin from TestGraph — one Scenario per case: "TC-… <title>", tags @P1 @<flow> @tg-<id>
    steps/<flow>.steps.ts                # step definitions: thin, call pages; no assertions hidden in pages
    steps/common.steps.ts                # steps shared by several features
    hooks/known-bugs.hooks.ts            # Before/After hooks (not glue): skips @intermittent known bugs in the normal run
  .features-gen/                         # generated by `bddgen` (git-ignored)
```
Imports use the aliases in `tsconfig.json` (`@fixtures`, `@pages/*`, `@support/*`, `@data/*`, `@utils/*`), not relative paths.

## Dependency injection (PicoContainer-style)
- A step asks for what it needs by name: `When('I save my alias', async ({ profilePage, ctx }) => …)`. It never does `new ProfilePage(page)`.
- Every fixture is **scenario-scoped**: created on first use, the **same instance** for every step of that scenario
  (across step files), and discarded at the end. `ctx` (`ScenarioContext`) is how steps share data.
- Nothing is shared between scenarios (no module-level variables, no statics, no singletons) → scenarios run **in parallel**
  (`fullyParallel: true`, one browser context per scenario).
- New Page Object → add it to `src/main/fixtures/index.ts` once; every step can then inject it.

## Run
```bash
cd e2e
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium
cp .env.example .env             # BASE_URL, local emulator URL, seed command
npm test                         # bddgen + playwright test (parallel)
npx bddgen && npx playwright test --grep @P1      # priority 1 · --grep @smoke · --grep @<flow>
npx bddgen && npx playwright test --workers=4     # parallelism
npm run steps                    # list every available step
npx playwright show-report       # HTML report · cucumber-report/index.html for the Gherkin view
```

## GritoGol specifics
- **App under test:** the docker compose stack of `gritogol/` (Vite dev server on 5173 + Firebase emulators: Firestore 8081,
  Auth 9099, Storage 9199, Functions 5001). `playwright.config.ts` `webServer` starts it in the foreground
  (`docker compose up --build`, cwd `..`) and runs `docker compose down` when Playwright stops it; if the app is already
  up on `BASE_URL` (e.g. `make start`), it is reused. Needs Docker and `make`.
- **Fresh data per scenario (`freshData` auto fixture):** empties the LOCAL Firestore emulator
  (`DELETE /emulator/v1/projects/gritogol/databases/(default)/documents`) and runs `make seed` before every scenario.
  `make seed` alone leaves videos and goal events (an open goal window re-opens the "¡GOOOL!" dialog). The client refuses
  any non-local host.
- **Serial run (`workers: 1`):** every scenario resets the one shared emulator and asserts match-wide counters
  ("pelotas" 47 → 48), so scenarios cannot overlap. They are still independent and order-agnostic.
- **Guests only:** no login. Each browser context is a new anonymous guest; the second fan of the applause case is a
  second context (`secondFan*` fixtures). Display names are unique per scenario (`QA Fan A <suffix>`).
- **Test data:** `src/main/data/files/celebration.webm` (~3 s WebM) is the video picked in the "Subir festejo" file chooser.
- **Short-lived UI states** ("El video está siendo revisado" ~40 ms, the applause rollback, toasts) are asserted with DOM
  observers armed before the action, not with sleeps.

## Reports of each run
| File | What for |
|---|---|
| `playwright-report/index.html` | Full report with traces, screenshots and video of failures |
| `cucumber-report/index.html` | Business-readable view: features, scenarios and steps |
| `test-results/junit.xml` | The CI's test view |
| `test-results/summary.md` / `.json` | Summary: passed, failed, flaky, known bugs (also in the GitHub job summary) |

## Known bugs
Scenarios tagged `@fail @BUG-NNN` reproduce confirmed product bugs (see the QACluster report): the suite stays green and the
bug stays visible. If one passes, the summary flags it as **bug fixed?**: verify it and remove both tags.

Scenarios tagged `@intermittent @BUG-NNN` reproduce product bugs that only show up some of the time. They are skipped in
`npm test` (summary: *known intermittent*) so they never turn CI red at random. `npm run test:intermittent` runs only them,
4 times each, and the summary shows the failure rate per bug (it exits non-zero while the bug reproduces; run it as a
non-blocking job). 0 failures out of 4 → **bug fixed?**: verify it and remove both tags. A bug that shows up very rarely
can pass 4 runs: verify by hand before removing the tags (or raise `--repeat-each` in the script).

## Maintenance
- `.qa-cluster.json` records what QACluster generated; files edited by people are not overwritten on the next run.
- CI: `ci/github-actions.yml`. The repo's root `.gitignore` ignores `.github/`; to enable the workflow, un-ignore
  `/.github/` and move the file to `<git root>/.github/workflows/qa-cluster-e2e.yml`.
- Feature files mirror TestGraph scenarios (exported as Gherkin from the dashboard). Change the behavior in TestGraph, not only here.
